newsitem.title: UK: NWE heating oil pressured, dollar slows trade.
newsitem.headline: NWE heating oil pressured, dollar slows trade.

text.p: European heating oil differentials were under pressure in slow business blighted by a strong dollar on Wednesday, traders said.
Outright prices firmed, with August IPE settling $2 a tonne higher at $164.75 on stronger U.S. products.
Business was thin and likely to remain so because of the dollar. While some buying was seen for early August the barge market picture was one of sellers struggling to find a trade.
First half August heating oil was done at August IPE +$0.50 with late July done at screen even.
Low sulphur diesel premiums were firm. A prompt barge was done basis Flushing at screen +$3.75. Rotterdam was $1 higher.
Diesel price rises due soon in Belgium because of the stronger dollar spurred end user interest. But traders said none of this extra demand had filtered into the ARA barge market.
Cargoes were stalled with sellers and buyers deadlocked. A first decade Hamburg heating oil offered at 75 cent over August IPE was at least 50 cents adrift of buyers.
A trade at $5 over the screen earlier in the week was seen distorting the low sulphur diesel market by inflating sellers' ideas. Buyers were at screen +$3.50.
